module_0_prerequisites.notes: Extremely strong at building intuition through analogy (neuroscience, software engineering composability, waterfall). Honest about uncertainty boundaries — flags when guessing vs knowing. Prefers concrete examples over abstraction.

strengths: Token embeddings — understands lookup from vocab to 768-dim vector, clear on what dimensionality buys you (resolution of concepts)

Positional encodings — understands why position-blind attention is broken (dog bites man vs man bites dog), grasps learned additive position vectors, correctly identified conflation risk as mostly a feature not a bug
Residual stream — solid grasp as shared communication bus, understands it's a vector (not matrix) that accumulates via addition, knows contributions are recoverable for interpretability

Q/K/V mechanics — strong understanding. Knows Q='what am I looking for', K='what should I be selected for', V='what I send when selected'. Understands all three are learned projections of the residual stream through shared weight matrices (768->64). Arrived at key != value insight through neurotransmitter analogy

Attention computation — understands dot product of Q and K for similarity scoring, scaling by sqrt(d_k) to prevent softmax saturation, softmax for weighting, weighted sum of V vectors as output. No binary match threshold, always continuous mixture

Multi-head attention — understands parallel independent heads as analogous to V1 orientation columns. 12 heads per layer, each with own W_Q/W_K/W_V/W_O. Gets that heads project from 768 to 64 dims (learned projection, not literal slice). Output projection W_O maps 64 back to 768
Shared weights across positions — clear that W_Q is same for all positions, input-dependence comes from different residual streams going in

MLP role — understands as two-layer network (768->3072->768) with GELU activation. Knows 4x expansion provides more feature detectors for intermediate computation. Understands universal approximation theorem motivation for two layers
Unembedding — understands matrix multiply of residual stream against embedding matrix to produce logits, logits as similarity scores, softmax to probabilities
LayerNorm — understands pre-norm placement (before attention and before MLP), learned scale/shift for restoring representational flexibility, purpose of stabilizing training
GELU vs ReLU — understands dying ReLU problem (dead neurons get zero gradient forever), GELU preserves small gradients for training stability
Full forward pass — can walk through embedding → (LayerNorm → attention → add → LayerNorm → MLP → add) × 12 → LayerNorm → unembedding → softmax

Math formalization — can write out attention score computation (q_t dot k_s / sqrt(d_k)), softmax, weighted sum of values, output projection, MLP equations. Understands all tensor shapes through the forward pass
Architecture design reasoning — understands dimension ratios (768/64/3072) as empirical conventions, asked about looped MLPs and independently arrived at Universal Transformer concept
gaps: OV circuit as separate concept — mentioned but not explored (Module 2 topic)
module_1_transformer_internals.build_challenge_description: Residual stream visualizer: load GPT-2 small via TransformerLens, extract residual stream at every layer, PCA to 2D, Plotly figure showing token trajectories through layers. CLI entry point: python -m visualizer.residual_stream 'The cat sat on the'. JSON export for blog embedding.
module_1_transformer_internals.notes: Conceptual understanding of Module 1 is strong — elevated to 'can_explain' status. Student can walk through the full forward pass both conceptually and mathematically. Neurotransmitter analogy for key vs value was a breakthrough. Showed strong architectural intuition by independently proposing looped MLPs (Universal Transformer concept). Distinguishes between architecture design questions (training dynamics) and mechanistic behavior questions (what the trained model does). Ready for build challenge.
